key_insight: A drilled-to-bossed joint geometry combined with optimized DDFW settings substantially improves AA2024-T351 weld strength, while deep learning can predict tensile performance from process conditions.
engineering_relevance: This work suggests a practical path to stronger lightweight metal joints for aerospace and automotive assembly by coupling joint-design modification with process optimization.
method: Used an L18 orthogonal array to study friction pressure, forging pressure, spindle speed, faying-surface geometry, and friction time.
Compared conventional flat-to-flat joints with a novel drilled-to-bossed geometry inspired by mortise-and-tenon interlocking.
Trained deep learning models (ensemble residual network, compact attention network, adaptive multiscale network) to predict ultimate tensile strength.
evidence_signal: The best condition reported 538 MPa tensile strength and 325 MPa torsional strength, and the top predictor achieved about R² = 0.81.
watch_item: The predictive model accuracy is moderate, so broader validation on more experiments and different alloy/joint configurations would be needed before deployment.
paper_title: Enhancing weld performance of AA2024-T351 using drilled-to-bossed geometry and deep learning prediction in direct drive friction welding
